headerDisplay: HomeKit control of an MG EV via the SAIC iSmart cloud API. Only one iSmart session is allowed at a time, so logging in here will sign the phone app out.
footerDisplay: Set the account password via a password file (mode 600) or the MG_SAIC_PASSWORD environment variable instead of pasting it into this form where possible, so it doesn't sit unencrypted in config.json on the NAS.

password.title: iSmart account password
password.description: Leave blank and use a password file or MG_SAIC_PASSWORD in the Homebridge environment instead, if possible.

passwordFile.title: Password file
passwordFile.description: Path to a file that holds only the password (owned by the Homebridge user, mode 600). Used when the password above is blank. Useful on Docker installs, where MG_SAIC_PASSWORD can't be set without recreating the container.

accessoryName.title: Accessory name
accessoryName.description: Name of the car accessory when it is first created. Defaults to the model name the account reports (e.g. MG4 EV, MGS6 EV). An existing accessory keeps its name; rename it in the Home app.

language.title: Tile names language
language.description: Language of the names the tiles get in the Home app (Cabin Heat / Chauffage habitacle, Driver door / Porte conducteur...). A tile you renamed in the Home app keeps your name.

commandDelaySeconds.title: Delay before a Home app change is sent (seconds)
commandDelaySeconds.description: A change in the Home app is answered at once and sent to the car only once nothing more has changed for this long, with the latest value: switching something on then off again within the delay sends nothing. A single change is always sent. 0 sends right away.

vin.title: Vehicle VIN (optional)
vin.description: Leave blank to use the first vehicle returned by the account. Set this if the account ever returns more than one vehicle, to pin the plugin to the primary MG4.

pollIntervalMinutes.title: Poll interval (minutes)
pollIntervalMinutes.description: SAIC's gateway can pause an account for 15 minutes if it sees too many logins. 15 minutes is the documented safe default.

enablePreconditioning.title: Expose cabin pre-conditioning (aircon) as Cabin Heat / Cabin Cool HeaterCoolers
enablePreconditioning.description: The remote aircon / climate control, exposed as a 'Cabin Heat' HeaterCooler tile (confirmed working on a real MG4), plus a separate 'Cabin Cool' tile only when the experimental option below is set (the compressor command was confirmed to heat at maximum on a real MG4, so without that option the Cool tile isn't shown). Each has its own target temperature slider, 17 °C to 33 °C on an MG4 (the range follows the vehicle series, see below). Turning one on automatically shows the other as off, since the car only has one underlying climate system. It is also not the pre-drive feature in the newer iSmart apps. See TESTING.md. With this off you get no tile in the Home app at all.

climateMinTemperature.title: Cabin Heat / Cabin Cool slider minimum (°C, optional)
climateMinTemperature.description: Leave blank to pick the range from the vehicle's series code, like saic-python-mqtt-gateway: MG4 (EH32) 17-33 °C, MG S5 (MZS3E) 16-31 °C, any other series 16-28 °C (the MG S6 EV lands here; its real range isn't confirmed), 17-33 °C if the series is unknown. Startup log shows the range in use.

climateMaxTemperature.title: Cabin Heat / Cabin Cool slider maximum (°C, optional)
climateMaxTemperature.description: Leave blank to pick it from the vehicle's series code (see the minimum above). Must be above the minimum.

enableExperimentalCabinCool.title: Experimental: let Cabin Cool start the climate without the compressor flag
enableExperimentalCabinCool.description: NOT confirmed on any real car. When on, turning Cabin Cool on sends the reference client's start_ac (fan 2 and the Cool tile's target temperature, no compressor flag), i.e. the same command as Cabin Heat, and relies on the car to cool towards a target below the cabin temperature. The raw remoteClimateStatus is logged on every change so you can see what the car actually did. Stay near the car the first time. See README.md.

enableDoorSensors.title: Expose door / boot / bonnet contact sensors

enableTemperatureSensors.title: Expose interior/exterior temperature sensors
enableTemperatureSensors.description: Off by default: temperature sensors appear on the iOS lock screen and Home widgets, which looks odd for car temperatures in a home context.

enableHeatedSeats.title: Expose heated seat switches (left/right)
enableHeatedSeats.description: Confirmed working against real hardware. Off by default since it's a newer control, see TESTING.md.

frontSeatHeatLevel.title: Front seat heat level when switched on

oneOf.title: 3 (high, the only level used before this option existed)

frontSeatHeatLevel.description: Level the left/right front seat heat switches send for On. Both front seats are set in one request, so a seat already on is restated at this level too.

enableRearHeatedSeats.title: Expose rear heated seat switches (rear left/rear right)
enableRearHeatedSeats.description: For cars with heated rear seats (e.g. MG S6 EV). Uses the reference client's per-seat command; rear seats are on/off only. Not yet confirmed against real hardware by this plugin. Off by default, see TESTING.md.

enableRearDefrost.title: Expose rear window defrost switch
enableRearDefrost.description: Confirmed working against real hardware. Off by default since it's a newer control, see TESTING.md.

enableFrontDefrost.title: Expose front window defrost switch
enableFrontDefrost.description: Not yet confirmed against real hardware. Off by default, see TESTING.md.

enableHeatedSteeringWheel.title: Expose heated steering wheel switch
enableHeatedSteeringWheel.description: On/off Switch for cars with a heated steering wheel (e.g. MG S6 EV), ported from the reference client. The car switches it off by itself after about 10 minutes. Not yet confirmed against real hardware by this plugin. Off by default, see TESTING.md.

enableWindowVentilation.title: Expose a window ventilation switch (MG S6 EV format)
enableWindowVentilation.description: One Switch for all four door windows, using the MG S6 EV's window command: on opens them a few centimetres, off closes them. Fully opening is not exposed. Reads on when any door window is open, including one opened by hand. The command format is confirmed on a real MG S6 EV (full open); the ventilate and close actions are not yet. Does not work on the MG4 (see README.md). Off by default.

enablePowerTailgate.title: Expose the power tailgate as a garage door opener
enablePowerTailgate.description: For cars with a power tailgate (e.g. MG S6 EV): open and close it from HomeKit. Exposed as a GarageDoorOpener rather than a Switch, so HomeKit treats it as a secure accessory and asks for confirmation before automations or Siri move it. Reads open/closed from the boot status, so it also shows Open when the boot was opened by hand. Not yet confirmed against real hardware by this plugin. Off by default, see TESTING.md.

useStatusCache.title: Experimental: routine polls read SAIC's stored status instead of waking the car
useStatusCache.description: Not yet tried on a real car. Every routine poll normally calls /vehicle/status, which wakes the car (every 15 minutes by default, a 12 V battery concern). With this on, routine polls read /vehicle/status/cache, the last status SAIC stored, without waking it. The full status is still read on the first poll, after any command, and whenever the cache lacks a field an enabled service needs - in the one capture available, the cache has no door or temperature fields, so with door or temperature sensors enabled it falls back every time (the log says so once). See README.md.
